reasons: F01, F03, F04, F05, F06, F07: no material weakness, clean ICFR opinion, no going concern, no auditor change or disagreements, and no prior-period correction, so the control environment looks sound.

F08, F09, F10, F11, F20, F26: no major over-time revenue, no significant contract assets, no return rights or bill-and-hold, no material related parties, no revenue/EPS-linked incentive pay and no non-GAAP emphasis, which limits the room for judgemental revenue manipulation.

R01, R18, R11, F12, F13: receivables grew 13 percentage points faster than sales (DSRI 1.10), a modest warning sign for revenue timing. Customer concentration is moderate (largest customer is 23% of revenue and 18% of receivables).

F14, F25: there was a CEO/CFO change in the year (without an interim CFO, F15) and a voluntary accounting change. Both are moderate flags that call for a review of the transition and the policy election, although a voluntary change is often an early adoption of a new standard.
